title: IBU-tec secures key approval for LFP production plant in Germany - electrive.com
content:
The German battery material specialist IBU-tec based in the state of Thuringa is making good progress with the construction of its LFP production facility in Bitterfeld-Wolfen. The supplier to VW battery subsidiary PowerCo has now received a key approval from the State Administration Office of Saxony-Anhalt, required to commence operations.
Topping-out ceremony of IBU-tec's spray tower (archive image)
Image: IBU-tec
The German battery maker
is currently constructing a new LFP production plant with a capacity of 15,000 tonnes at its site in Bitterfeld-Wolfen, scheduled to begin operations in 2028. A significant milestone was already celebrated in April with the
topping-out ceremony for the new spray tower
The plant is linked to the strategy of PowerCo, Volkswagen’s battery subsidiary that produces the unified cell. PowerCo SE has already secured the entire LPF plant’s production capacity for 10 years at pre-defined prices. For IBU-tec, this is expected to generate annual revenue in the mid- to high double-digit millions starting in 2028, in the profitable segment. During the transition phase, IBU-tec will begin producing LFP cathode material for PowerCo this year using existing facilities at its headquarters in Weimar, continuing until 2028.
IBU-tec has now received the necessary approval from the State Administration Office of Saxony-Anhalt for new operational buildings to establish the production platform for battery materials at the Bitterfeld-Wolfen site. According to the company, the approved building complex also includes a new, state-of-the-art laboratory for battery materials made from various material combinations.
IBU-tec achieves multiple milestones
IBU-tec states that it has already achieved several milestones in Bitterfeld-Wolfen over the past few months. These include the development of logistics infrastructure, the expansion of analytical capabilities, and the harmonisation of IT systems, all progressing according to the established timeline. The company has also commenced detailed engineering for the production facilities and erected the steel structure for a logistics hall with a storage capacity of approximately 2,000 pallets on the site. The interior construction is expected to be completed by the end of the year, with the trial operation of the spray tower scheduled for the end of Q4.
IBU-tec expects the new LFP production plant to become operational in early 2028. According to the company, IBU-tec will then be the only provider in Europe capable of producing LFP cathode material on an industrial scale. While PowerCo SE has already secured access to the full production output for ten years, IBU-tec also highlights other potential applications for the battery material, including stationary battery storage and certain areas of defence technology.

title: Lanxess commissions battery laboratory for LFP materials in Germany - electrive.com
content:
Lanxess has opened a new battery laboratory at its Krefeld-Uerdingen site in Germany. The specialty chemicals company plans to test and further develop its materials for LFP batteries directly in battery cells.
Lanxess is testing materials for LFP cathodes directly in battery cells in its new battery laboratory.
Image: Lanxess
is expanding its activities in materials for lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. The new battery laboratory in Krefeld-Uerdingen focuses primarily on iron oxides and iron phosphate that serve as raw materials for LFP cathode materials. With its new equipment, Lanxess says it can directly examine the properties of its materials in cell construction. Among other things, the company aims to investigate the way different grades of iron oxide and iron phosphate affect cell performance, processing, and suitability for specific applications. The company expects this to lead to shorter development cycles and faster evaluation of new materials in collaboration with its customers.
Lanxess has not disclosed details regarding the investment amount, the laboratory’s capacity, or specific customer projects. The company has also not yet provided performance data for the materials being tested there. However, the technical equipment is not limited to LFP technology. According to Lanxess, it can also examine materials for other cell chemistries, such as sodium iron pyrophosphate as a cathode material for sodium-ion batteries.
Lanxess is not new to developing such materials. As early as the beginning of 2024, the speciality chemicals company launched a
research cooperation with IBU-Tec
. The two companies aimed to further develop iron oxides specifically for LFP cathode materials, enabling improvements in energy density, charging speed, and cycle stability, among other things. The partners have said they aim to establish a European value chain for LFP materials.
In the meantime, Lanxess has, according to its own statements, developed special iron oxide grades for battery applications and introduced them to the market as ‘Battery Grades’. Iron phosphate is yet another precursor for LFP cathode materials. The manufacturing process developed by Lanxess is based on iron and phosphoric acid and is said to produce less saline wastewater than established processes. However, the company does not provide specific comparative figures for this environmental advantage.
Lanxess entwickelt Eisenoxide und Eisenphosphat als Ausgangsstoffe für Kathodenmaterialien von LFP-Batterien.
Lanxess continues to expand LFP activities
The new laboratory now complements this material development with its own cell tests. This allows Lanxess to assess its raw materials not only based on their chemical and physical properties but also to investigate how they behave in cell construction. For a chemical company that does not itself act as a cell manufacturer, this is particularly relevant for the development and qualification of its precursor materials.
The company’s expansion is also driven by the growing importance of LFP chemistry. Lanxess refers to figures from Roland Berger, according to which LFP batteries could achieve a market share of 50 per cent in Europe by 2030, compared to around ten per cent today. In addition to electric cars, the company sees stationary energy storage systems, data centres, and critical infrastructure as further growth drivers.
At the same time, Lanxess aims to position itself as a supplier for Western battery value chains with its materials. The company already has large-scale iron oxide production and describes itself as a leading Western manufacturer of the material. The company’s current public statement does not specify the size of the production capacities for battery applications or the extent to which its Battery Grades are already being used commercially.
Beyond LFP precursors, Lanxess is already active in other areas of the battery value chain. The German company’s portfolio includes, among other things, chemicals for electrolyte salts, ion exchange resins for the extraction and refining of lithium, nickel, and cobalt, as well as solutions for thermal management and flame retardancy. For battery recycling, the company also offers process chemicals and ion exchange resins for the processing of black mass, metal recovery, and wastewater treatment.
With the new battery laboratory, Lanxess primarily aims to expand its development and testing expertise for battery materials. It remains to be seen whether this will also lead to larger production volumes or specific supply contracts for LFP precursors.

title: ProLogium begins series production of next-generation solid-state batteries in Taiwan - electrive.com
content:
Taiwanese solid-state battery specialist ProLogium is starting series production of its Generation 3.5 lithium-ceramic battery in Taiwan. According to ProLogium, the multinational German organisation for certifying vehicular standards, TÜV Rheinland, has confirmed that the cells used achieve a gravimetric energy density of 381 Wh/kg.
ProLogium showcases its range of lithium-ceramic batteries.
Image: ProLogium
ProLogium
, a Taiwan-based specialist in lithium-ceramic batteries (LCB), has announced the start of series production for its ‘Generation 3.5’. This generation is based on all-
solid-state battery
technology and, according to a report by TÜV Rheinland, achieves a gravimetric energy density of 381 Wh/kg and a volumetric energy density of 903 Wh/L at the cell level. The tests were conducted on a large-format 185.4 Ah cell.
The new solid-state battery also underwent testing at the U.S. testing laboratory UL Solutions, which examined the cell according to the Chinese standard GB/T 43568-2026, as stated by ProLogium in a press release, though no further test details were provided. The company only noted that the cell lost less than 0.05 % of its weight after six hours under vacuum at 120 °C—meaning it can be classified as a solid-state battery in accordance with the standard.
Since its founding in 2006, ProLogium has focused on lithium-ceramic batteries and holds over 1,200 patents worldwide (including granted and pending patents). In 2013, the company commercialised its solid-state battery technology in the smartphone charging accessories market. However, since 2022, the automotive industry has also become a key focus, as ProLogium obtained IATF 16949 certification for its production line in Taiwan that year.
ProLogium has used the underlying battery cell platform (the “Logithium” cell architecture) since 2012. This is because the architecture remains compatible even as electrolyte chemistry and active materials evolve. Now, ProLogium has refined the manufacturing processes and material compositions — not the fundamental design. The architecture consistently combines a ceramic separator with a proprietary edge frame structure, creating an additional separator around the electrodes that helps isolate potential burrs (i.e., defects) while ensuring sealing and insulation.
Since 2012, ProLogium has built on this foundation to develop four generations of batteries and three generations of manufacturing technology. The aforementioned Generation 3.5 has now entered series production. However, the company is already working on commercialising the fourth generation. While automakers are a target group, they are far from the only one.
An explicit goal in the progression of these generations is the gradual reduction of organic electrolyte content. The “Gen 4 LCB” is set to establish a new benchmark by incorporating a “fully inorganic, superfluidised electrolyte system,” as ProLogium states. Currently, the company estimates that only about 10 % of the existing gigascale production line and associated equipment will need to be adjusted to manufacture Gen 4 cells. The fourth generation is expected to improve performance at low temperatures, reduce material and production costs, and introduce a new safety layer with ProLogium’s ASM (“Active Safety Mechanism”).
In North America, single-layer core units of the cell (“inlays”) from France will initially be used in local assembly into pouch cells with local partners through simple direct stacking. ProLogium plans to expand and build production capacity in Taiwan, France, and North America. Module and pack integration will follow.
In France, ProLogium officially began construction of its factory in Dunkerque, northern France,
in February 2026
, as announced in 2023. The first phase, focused on producing fourth-generation solid-state batteries with an initial annual capacity of 0.8 GWh, is scheduled for completion in 2028. The existing factory in Taoyuan, Taiwan, has a capacity of 3 GWh. From 2029, capacity in Dunkerque will be ramped up so that, by 2030 in Phase 2, the facilities will operate at full utilisation with 4 GWh per year. By 2032, the “Fab 1” plant is expected to reach its full capacity of 12 GWh.

title: How is Checkpoint Systems Unlocking Supply Chain Efficiency?
content:
How is Checkpoint Systems Unlocking Supply Chain Efficiency?
Prioritise Us
on Google
Checkpoint is attending RAIN in Action 2026 as a Gold Sponsor (Credit: Getty)
Checkpoint Systems is participating in RAIN in Action 2026, working to unlock sustainability and efficiency with RFID technology
As technology advances, businesses are increasingly looking at where they can use it for sustainability purposes.
Around the world, supply chain leaders are looking to integrate efficiency and responsible solutions across their operations, particularly as leaders are seeing the economic benefit of clear sustainability initiatives.
Checkpoint is constantly working to use technology to solve modern and real-world supply chain challenges. To do so, it is participating as a Gold Sponsor in RAIN in Action 2026.
Growing technologies
RAIN in Action 2026 is a three-day event of end-user case studies, live technology demonstrations and hands-on workshops. The event explores how RAIN technology can have an impact on supply chains, operating as a must-attend event for any leader planning to deploy RAIN technology. It will be taking place in Madrid, with the event kicking off on 29 September.
RAIN technology is a standards-based, wireless technology. It ensures trillions of everyday items are connecting to the internet, which allows businesses to operate at full capacity. Through this technology, businesses and consumers can identify, locate, authenticate and engage each item.
It is the fastest-growing part of the
RFID market
– in 2024, more than one billion
RAIN chips
were shipped every week. It helps identify and locate items, even without direct line of sight. Through this, the process is much faster and more efficient. Alongside this, it can identify up to 1,000 items per second, making the processing of inventory much more streamlined.
RAIN technology provides real-time data and insights across applications,
inventory management
, asset tracking and supply chain optimisation. Its Tags can be embedded within items, storing and sending information to leaders, with accuracy.
RFID can capture item-level information. Credit: Checkpoint
Checkpoint and RFID
For Checkpoint, the event acts as a perfect opportunity to explore new technology, but more importantly – to look at the data driving every product. Checkpoint, as a Gold Sponsor, will be looking at the latest key trends which are bringing RAIN RFID into the future.
According to Checkpoint, the technology acts as a foundation for sustainable, data-driven supply chains, helping to reduce overproduction, waste and excess inventory. Using the technology, supply chains can get unparalleled levels of visibility into their inventory, meaning greater accuracy and productivity.
At the event, attendees will be exploring how to gain product-level transparency using the technology, gaining the ability to support circular logistics and food traceability. Through this, supply chain leaders are able to use thorough insights and turn them into smarter, more efficient operational decisions.
In today's world of changing policy, greater scrutiny and evolving regulatory standards, reliable information is a necessity. RAIN RFID makes trustworthy data accessible, helping businesses meet compliance requirements with confidence, which translates to
more efficient
and successful operational performances.
“We see RAIN RFID moving far beyond inventory counting. It gives products and assets the intelligence needed to reduce waste, improve traceability and support more circular chains,” says Inge Fleuren, Global Product Manager RFID consumables at Checkpoint Systems.
Inge Fleuren, Global Product Solutions Manager RFID at Checkpoint Systems
"At RAIN in Action Madrid, we look forward to discussing how the RFID ecosystem can turn item-level data into practical progress for businesses, supply chains and sustainability.”
Technological capabilities
RFID technology
has already been used extensively across the retail sector, proving invaluable for its inventory accuracy. Now, it is being introduced into more sectors, helping a wider set of industries capture reliable item-level data. Organisations around the world are using the technology to track, manage and reuse assets and products at a more effective level.
As the items are being given a unique digital identity, they are easier to follow across their lifecycle. Through this, companies can act more efficiently and sustainably with assets which often fall under the radar –
traceability
allows for the reuse of pallets, crates and reusable containers. This cuts avoidable waste and is significantly more cost effective, as organisations do not need to buy new containers for each delivery.
Checkpoint, as a result, is looking to unpack this and more at RAIN in Action.

title: VW's new ID. Polo is apparently sold out, with over 30,000 orders and a 10-month waitlist
content:
Volkswagen
Peter Johnson
| Sep 7 2026 - 8:45 am PT
Volkswagen’s
new ID. Polo EV is apparently sold out after receiving over 30,000 orders. Buyers are now being told it will be at least a 10-month wait.
Is the Volkswagen ID. Polo sold out?
Volkswagen is betting on its new family of electric city cars to fight back against Chinese automakers like BYD.
So far, it’s apparently off to a promising start. After
opening orders for the ID. Polo
at the end of April, the entry-level EV has received more than 30,000 orders ahead of its official launch.
According to German newspaper
Automobilwoche
, the VW ID. Polo is already sold out across all trims. The head of a larger VW dealership said the waitlist for the electric city car has now reached at least 10 months.
Volkswagen confirmed the report, telling
Automobilwoche
that the response has been “very positive,” but it’s leading to longer-than-expected delivery delays.
“Everyone is switching to electric cars they can afford,” a dealership group executive said. The base
VW ID. Polo Trend
with the 37 kWh battery, starts at just €24,995, or about $29,000, and offers a WLTP range of 334 km (207 miles).
Volkswagen ID. Polo Trend (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen is ramping up production to meet higher-than-expected demand at its Martorell plant in Spain.
The Skoda Epiq and Cupra Raval, which share the same MEB+ platform and are built at the same facility, are facing a similar situation.
Volkswagen ID. Polo and Cupra Raval enter production at SEAT & CUPRA plant in Martorell (Source: Volkswagen)
According to company sources, Volkswagen’s entry-level electric SUV, the ID. Cross, is also seeing strong initial demand. VW
opened orders for the ID. Cross
, the electric counterpart to its best-selling T-Cross in Europe, in July, starting at €27,995 in Germany, or roughly $32,000.
Electrek’s Take
While the initial response to Volkswagen’s new lineup of lower-priced electric city cars has been stronger than expected, the company still faces an uphill battle.
Volkswagen’s supervisory board
approved its Future Plan 2030
last week, calling for additional job cuts (up to 100,000 globally), a trimmed model lineup, and more plant closures.
The restructuring package comes as the German automaker aims to cut costs and keep pace with Chinese brands, like BYD, that are leading the auto industry’s shift to electric.

title: If a Tesla Cybercab fleet were profitable, Tesla wouldn't sell you one
content:
Robotaxi
Fred Lambert
| Sep 7 2026 - 7:38 am PT
Tesla is now asking businesses whether they’d like to buy and operate their own fleets of Cybercab robotaxis on its network. It’s the same pitch Elon Musk has been making since 2019: buy the cars, put them to work, and earn money while you sleep.
There’s one problem with it. And it never happened, and you shouldn’t fall for it now. If running a fleet of Cybercabs were actually profitable, Tesla wouldn’t sell you a single one.
The pitch Tesla keeps making
At its Cybercab event on September 3, Tesla started
circulating an interest form to fleet buyers
asking who wants in on “Cybercab fleet vehicle purchasing.” The idea is that a company buys the cars, runs them on Tesla’s Robotaxi network, and splits the revenue.
We’ve heard this before. At Autonomy Day in 2019, Musk told the world that owners could add their cars to the “Tesla Network” and pull in as much as $30,000 a year in gross profit per vehicle. Same year, he called Teslas
“appreciating assets”
that would gain value as Full Self-Driving improved.
None of it happened. Owners paid up to $15,000 for FSD on the promise of taxi income, and years later,
not one of them can run their car as a robotaxi
. Tesla runs the service itself. The people who funded the dream are still waiting.
Ask MisterGreen how that worked out
Some people actually built a business on Musk’s promise. MisterGreen, a Dutch leasing firm, went all-in on Tesla, buying
more than 4,000 of them
on the belief that the cars would hold their value and eventually earn robotaxi income.
Instead, Tesla spent two years slashing new-car prices, and used Teslas started depreciating at roughly three times the rate of the broader used-car market. The robotaxi income never came. MisterGreen went bankrupt in December 2025 and wiped out its bondholders. $40 million was lost.
That’s what betting on the “appreciating asset” looks like in practice. Not great.
Why selling you a robotaxi is the tell
Tesla is not a charity. It aims to maximize profits. Tesla builds the Cybercab. It owns the Robotaxi network, the software, the dispatch, and the pricing. It sets the split. If a Cybercab on that network genuinely printed $30,000 a year, why would Tesla hand that money to a stranger instead of keeping every car for itself?
Companies don’t outsource money machines. They outsource risk. Selling you the Cybercab means you eat the capital cost and the depreciation, while Tesla keeps the software margin and its cut of every fare.
And you’d be competing directly against the company that controls the platform. Tesla can undercut your prices, prioritize its own cars in the app, change the revenue split, or geofence you out entirely. You don’t own a business in that arrangement. You own the downside.
Electrek’s Take
This is asset-light offloading dressed up as an opportunity. Tesla wants fleet buyers to absorb the capex and the depreciation on hundreds of thousands of Cybercabs so it can book the vehicle sale, keep the high-margin software, and skim the network. The risk moves to you. The margin stays with Tesla.
It’s the FSD playbook again. Sell the promise of future income, collect the money up front, and let the buyer hold the bag when the economics don’t materialize. MisterGreen is the case study, and it’s barely nine months old.
I also know of another company that built a Tesla fleet in LA in 2018-2020 in preparation for the infamous ‘Tesla Network’ revenue that never materialized. They had to shut down shortly after.
If robotaxi fleets were the goldmine Musk describes, Tesla is sitting on the cash, the factories, and the network to run them all itself and never share a dollar. Instead, it’s passing around the gold out of the goodness of its heart. Please. That should tell you everything about who’s meant to carry the risk here. So before anyone signs up to buy a fleet of Cybercabs, the question worth asking is simple: if this is such easy money, why is Tesla so eager to let you have it?

title: Review: Engwe's $900 Eagle isn't just the best-priced 45mph mini eMoto
content:
Seth Weintraub
| Sep 7 2026 - 7:10 am PT
Engwe came to us a month ago with the
and asked if we’d like to review it. The eMoto looks and is specced a lot like some of the other 14/12″ mullet mini eMotos that have flooded the market over the past year, which wasn’t immediately enticing. However, the Eagle smashes through that $1000 price point to
$899 after coupon code ELECTREKCO (plus some limited-time gifts)
. We thought it would be useful to see how they did it and what we found might surprise you.
Engwe is a brand
we’ve reviewed before and has a
track record
of building solid value ebikes.
The Eagle builds on the small Tuttio/Yozma 14/12-inch wheel form factor that has become incredibly popular for pre-teens and teens throughout the US. These are obviously off-road bikes and aren’t legal on the road in almost any jurisdiction. The spec sheet will look somewhat familiar:
3200W Peak Mid-drive Motor
F14″/R12″ Off-Road Tires
Top Speed
Waterproof Rating
Maximum Range
55 Miles(Throttle Mode)
52V 27Ah Lithium-Ion Battery
200mm Hydraulic Disc Brakes
Suspension
Full Suspension
Maximum Climbing Degree
Charging Time
5-6 Hours (3A Charger)
Front Light
LED Headlight
LCD Display
Max Load Capacity
Bike Weight
Material
High carbon steel
Note the higher 220nm torque than not just Tuttio and Yozma, but even the higher-end Heybike Villan. That’s going to get you off the line, up the hill, and into a wheelie much better than higher-priced bikes. The 3.2kW motor falls in the midrange between Yozma (2.6kW) and Heybike (4.2kW), but the stated range of 55 miles is higher than both. Obviously, 1.4kWh battery range estimates are highly subjective, and in the real world, going 28mph you’ll get 30-35 miles, give or take, depending on rider weight, terrain, weather, and other factors. We reviewed the red option, but I think the Black and Gray version might be the star here:
Engwe Eagle differentiators
I wasn’t expecting to love the trade-offs for getting to a sub $900 price point. But they are actually quite remarkable. First of all, there are no keys. Instead, you can remove power from the moto by taking the red kill switch off (an easily replaceable safety feature as well). The seat is removable with a big screw at the bottom, and the battery is secured with a heavy-duty strap. This isn’t going to prevent theft, but it also isn’t going to hinder your experience if you lose your keys.
Also, Engwe forgoes the Fardriver controller that many of these eMotos use and has a custom setup (which very well could be a Fardriver controller on lockdown). While that restricts Bluetooth access to program the controller, it also lets Engwe deliver a strong mix of torque, power, and range that beats other bikes in its class. You can also access the P-settings menu, which allows users to restrict top speed, switch between kilometers and miles, adjust backlighting, and change sleep and other settings.
The 4.7-inch big, waterproof color display is surprisingly one of the best we’ve seen, with large, high-contrast, readable speed/ride mode (0-3), Battery meter, status, and odometer numbers. The left-hand, 5-button thumb controller is also very usable, and both the horn and front headlight are perfectly usable safety features.
I was also pleasantly surprised by how easy the Eagle was to assemble. Engwe made the kickstand and pegs very easy to install, and the rest of the eMoto probably took us about 30 mins to put together. With an ~80% charged battery, we were ripping within an hour of the box landing on our doorstep.
Reality mode:
Look, this is a sub-
$900 eMoto so don’t expect a $1000 suspension package on here.
As a 200-lb rider, I bottomed out a few times on the trails, and the suspension was probably as baseline as it gets. At 6 feet tall, riding it felt cramped, as a friend tells me on these bikes; I seem a little bit like a circus clown attempting a high-wire act.
However, for my much lighter son, this is actually a pretty incredible ride. No complaints on the hills, though we were hesitant to bring it near significant jumps.
Engwe includes a 3A charger which charges the bike in 5-6 hours, with an optional $99 8A charger that drops charging time to 2-3 hours. That’s great and better than some competitors, but the charging head is proprietary, and it isn’t interchangeable with other electronics, which is a bit frustrating.
Like all of these eMotos, a top speed of 45 mph is attainable only under optimal conditions (like a slight downhill, crouch, and tailwind), but hitting 40 on a dirt straightaway is very possible, especially for lighter riders, and I’m sure that with enduro tires 45mph is doable. In reality, you’ll be tooling around mostly in the high 30s, which is still lots of fun and probably a lot safer than going highway speeds.
Speaking of safety, any kid riding an emoto hard should be wearing lots of safety gear and much beefier stuff than is included in the Engwe package. Also, in reality, kids are going to take these on roads whether that’s just around the neighborhood or down the road to get to the dirt track, so they should be fully protected and schooled in safety protocols.
Electrek’s take
I’m still blown away at this package at this price. The Eagle is one of the better 14/12 eMotos out there at any price, and the fact that you can pick up a 45mph electric bike for $899 from a reputable brand from US storefronts is bananas. It bodes well for the future of electric transportation if we can get homologated street bikes out to the masses at these prices.
At $900, I expected a glaring disappointment compared to the other emotos in its class, which are as much as $500 more, but instead found that Engwe managed some nice improvements (torque, display, controls, kill switch) over its competitors with very little in sacrifices (suspension?). If you are 6’+ and 200lbs like me, I’d
recommend hitting up a bigger bike like this Qronge.
But 5’9/180lbs and under? Pick up the
Engwe Eagle for $899 using code Electrekco
at checkout to receive a bunch of gifts (currently pictured below), or at
Amazon without gifts by clicking the $100 off box
. Labor Day weekend only.

title: Audi reveals its new entry-level EV with over 400 miles of range starts at about $45,000
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 7 2026 - 6:46 am PT
The A2 e-tron is
most efficient vehicle ever, delivering over 400 miles of range. It’s also the brand’s affordable model, positioned as its new entry-level EV.
Audi A2 e-tron prices and EV range
original Audi A2
, which went on sale over 25 years ago, became known as the “world’s first four-door three-liter car” for its lightweight, ultra-efficient compact design.
Audi is bringing back the A2 name, and this time, it’s even more efficient with an all-electric powertrain.
The A2 e-tron has an energy consumption of just 12.8 kWh/ 100 km, according to WLTP, making it the most efficient series-production Audi of all time.
After unveiling the new entry-level EV for the first time on Monday, CEO Gernot Döllner said the A2 e-tron is “more than a new model,” calling it the brand’s “renewal.”
With a drag coefficient of just 0.24, the A2 e-tron (140 kW) has a WLTP range of up to 401 miles (646 km). It will be available with four power levels: 125 kW, 140 kW, 170 kW, and 240 kW, plus three battery sizes: 52, 61, or 84 kWh.
Audi A2 e-tron (Source: Audi)
Despite being an entry-level model, the A2 e-tron supports bidirectional charging, enabling it to power external electronics via Vehicle-to-Load (V2L). In Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, it can also be used as a backup home battery with a DC wall box via Vehicle-to-Home (V2H).
With DC fast-charging speeds of up to 183 kW, the 84 kWh battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes.
Audi A2 e-tron interior (Source: Audi)
The 52 kWh LFP battery takes about 14 minutes at up to 100 kW, while the 61 kWh battery takes 25 minutes at up to 105 kW.
Audi included several driver-assist features as standard, including Emergency brake assist, swerve assist, attention assist, adaptive cruise control (ACC), parking system plus, and a reversing camera.
Audi A2 e-tron interior (Source: Audi)
At just 4.32 meters (170″) long and 1.79 meters (70.5″) wide, with a wheelbase of 2.77 meters (109″), the A2 e-tron is about the size of the
and Volkswagen ID.3 Neo.
The smart storage and premium features make the interior feel more spacious despite its compact size.
Audi is the first luxury brand to offer the Fidlock fastening system, a patented magnetic smart storage solution, as standard. You can also opt for the optional panoramic glass roof with 1.6 square meters of glass across the roof.
Audi A2 e-tron (Source: Audi)
Orders will open on September 10, 2026, starting at €38,200 ($45,000) in Germany, for the base A2 e-tron 125 kW with the 52 kWh battery.
The 61 kWh variant starts at €41,900, while the A2 e-tron with 170 kW and the 84 kWh battery costs €48,900. The range-topping A2 e-tron 240 kW starts at €51,200.
Audi is building the A2 e-tron at its Ingolstadt plant in Germany. The first customer deliveries are expected to begin in December 2026.
Will Audi bring the entry-level EV to the US? It hasn’t been confirmed yet, but don’t get your hopes up. The A2 is built in Germany specifically for the European market.

title: Evoke’s new $5,000 electric motorcycle can hit highway speeds, coming to US & EU
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 7 2026 - 6:30 am PT
Electric motorcycles have long had a pricing problem. While battery-powered scooters and e-bikes have increasingly pushed into affordable territory, highway-capable electric motorcycles still tend to carry fairly hefty price tags.
Evoke Motorcycles
is hoping to change that with its newly unveiled 2027 Evoke Nrgy, a lightweight electric motorcycle targeting a starting price of just $4,995.
And unlike many lower-cost electric two-wheelers, this one is actually designed to handle the highway.
The new Evoke Nrgy tops out at 120 km/h (75 mph), putting it comfortably above typical urban electric motorcycles and scooters and giving riders enough speed for a mix of city, suburban, and highway riding.
That aligns it with other popular light electric motorcycles like
Ryvid Anthem,
going beyond the realm of overpowered electric mopeds and allowing true highway jaunts.
Evoke plans to offer the bike in two versions. The Nrgy 6 gets a 6.4 kWh battery and carries that targeted US $4,995 starting price, while the Nrgy 8 bumps the battery capacity up to 8.4 kWh and is expected to start at US $6,495.
Interestingly, both use lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells instead of the more energy-dense chemistries commonly found in electric motorcycles. LFP batteries generally trade some energy density for advantages including improved thermal stability, longer cycle life, and potentially lower costs.
Evoke hasn’t yet announced range figures for either model, so we’ll have to wait to see just how far those fairly sizable packs can carry the Nrgy. But with battery packs landed squarely in the ‘modest’ category, these bikes will likely be best suited for urban riding with some short but fun higher speed sections thrown in – not long distance touring.
The bike is built around Evoke’s patented Twin Plate chassis architecture and features disc brakes at both ends. The styling is also fairly distinctive, with large slab-sided body panels surrounding the battery area, a traditional-looking faux tank up top, and a minimalist tail. It’s an interesting mix of futuristic electric motorcycle design with some conventional motorcycle cues, and appears to draw some inspiration from the previous 6061 model we saw from Evoke
several years ago.
“The Evoke Nrgy fills an important gap in our global product portfolio,” explained Evoke CEO Nathan Siy, adding that the company aimed to create a lightweight electric motorcycle without sacrificing “performance, safety or build quality.”
The company is positioning the Nrgy as a global model, targeting Southeast Asia, Europe, and North America. Final regional pricing, homologation details, preorder timing, and delivery schedules are expected to be announced in the coming months.
At $5,000, the Nrgy could find itself in an interesting position, assuming it meets its pricing goals. That’s still considerably more expensive than the growing crop of high-powered electric bikes and e-motos, but it’s getting into a much more approachable price range for something capable of legitimate highway speeds.
Of course, that $5k figure is still a
price, and we’ve yet to see range figures or final regional specifications. But if the Beijing-based company can actually deliver a 75 mph electric motorcycle with a 6.4 kWh LFP battery in the US for around five grand, that combination could make lightweight electric motorcycles a lot easier to justify.

title: 1927-2027: Volvo celebrates 100 years with special-edition electric semi
content:
Commercial EVs
Electric Semi Truck
Jo Borrás
| Sep 7 2026 - 6:00 am PT
Volvo is celebrating its 100th anniversary with launch of a new, special edition Volvo FH16 Electric semi truck featuring special paint, interior upgrades, and a promise from the company to keep on keepin’ on for at least 100 more.
Volvo’s heavy-duty truck range has become safer, more powerful,
and more energy efficient with the launch of the latest FH and FH16 Electric models
– and the company is celebrating that century of progress with a unique new 100 Year Edition for its FH line featuring two-tone exterior design, a premium leather seat base with special 100 Year Edition embroidered on the grey textile of the upper half, and tan leather details that match the anniversary edition striping details on the truck’s paintwork.
“This special edition represents the peak of Volvo’s truck design and manufacture over the past century,” says Jan Hjelmgren, Head of Product Management at Volvo Trucks. “(It is) the result of 100 years’ worth of continual improvement in safety, quality, driver comfort, productivity, fuel efficiency and emissions saving.”
Details matter
The special-edition Volvo get unique illuminated doorsteps and LED strips on the console, switchable between red and white ambient mood lighting. An LED welcome light projects the 100 Year Edition branding onto the ground when the door opens, and the same design shows up on 3D-printed speaker grilles. Special sleeper cab curtains (shown, below) display a timeline of Volvo’s key truck models from the past century, and a thicker, more luxurious floor mat in a black/grey mélange with tan leather labels rounds out the interior upgrades.
Sexy sleeper curtains
100 Year Edition cab curtain; by Volvo.
“The 100-year edition truck is a celebration of what we have achieved so far over the past century, and a very special truck in more ways than one,” explains Volvo Trucks’ Design Director, Jonathan Disley. “The interior is both modern and premium, as well as an homage to Volvo’s history. The design was inspired by our Swedish heritage and the professionalism that comes from years of innovation and progress, alongside our customers’ trust and passion.”
The Volvo 100 Year Edition FH is the latest in a storied line of special edition Volvo models, which have previously included the Volvo FH 25 Year Special Edition, the Volvo FH Aero Euro NCAP Special Edition, and the Volvo Ocean Race Limited Edition.
The truck, itself
Volvo FH16 Electric 100 Year Edition.
The Volvo FH Electric offers fleets up to 540 kW
(~730 hp) of peak power from its advanced eAxles,
which get their electrons from a 360 kWh battery pack
(up to 780 kWh are available). That combination is good for up to 400 km (~250 miles) of loaded range and can be recharge from 20% to 80% in about an hour on “just” 350 kW of charging power, enabling the truck to effectively “top off” at stops, between shift changes, or while its trailer is being loaded or un-loaded.
Pricing for the new 100 Year Edition trim level wasn’t announced, but the order books are open, so I’m sure your dealer can tell you all about it.

title: Italy deploys 2.61 GW of solar in H1 - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Italy added 2.9 GW of renewable energy capacity in the first half of 2026, with solar accounting for 2.6 GW. Cumulative PV capacity reached approximately 46.8 GW at the end of June.
Massimiliano Tripodo
07 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
Residential
Utility-scale
Florence, Italy
Renewable energy installations in Italy returned to growth in the second quarter of 2026, rising 14% year on year after six months of contraction. The rebound was driven almost entirely by solar, which grew 18%, according to renewable energy association ANIE Rinnovabili, citing data from Italian grid operator Terna.
Italy connected 83,791 new renewable energy systems in the first half of 2026, totaling 2,918 MW of capacity. Solar accounted for around 90% of the new capacity, with 83,732 systems totaling 2,610.9 MW. Wind followed with 295.2 MW, bioenergy with 7.4 MW and hydropower with 5.4 MW.
Solar capacity additions rose 18% year on year, while wind and hydropower declined 22% and 73%, respectively. Bioenergy additions increased 94%, albeit from low and uneven volumes.
Performance varied across solar market segments. Residential installations continued to slow for the third consecutive year, falling 22% from the previous quarter and 20% year on year. The commercial and industrial (C&I) segment remained broadly stable, rising 1% quarter on quarter and 8% on a rolling 12-month basis.
Utility-scale installations declined 12% from the first quarter. Installations of projects larger than 10 MW, however, surged 197% quarter on quarter, following limited activity in the first quarter, and increased 12% on a rolling 12-month basis.
Italy added 1,523 MW of solar in the second quarter, up from 1,395 MW in the first quarter, representing a 9% quarter-on-quarter increase. The additions brought cumulative installed solar capacity to approximately 46.8 GW at the end of June.
ANIE Rinnovabili also highlighted significant regional differences. Puglia, Sicily and Lazio remained among Italy’s most active regions, supported by large-scale projects, while deployment in Lombardy and Veneto continued to be driven by small- and medium-sized solar installations.
Italy needs to add another 3.3 GW of renewable energy capacity in the second half of 2026 to meet its annual target of 8.3 GW, roughly matching deployment during the first six months of the year.
ANIE Rinnovabili said the target remains within reach, but meeting it would exhaust the buffer accumulated between 2021 and 2025. That would leave Italy with little margin as annual deployment requirements rise to 10 GW in 2027, 11 GW in 2028, 13 GW in 2029 and 15 GW in 2030.
“The last two years have been a particularly complex period for the renewable energy sector,” said Andrea Cristini, president of ANIE Rinnovabili, citing “profound legislative and regulatory changes” as a source of uncertainty.
The association called for measures to address permitting bottlenecks, accelerate environmental assessments for 13 GW of projects awaiting review by the Prime Minister’s Office, and establish a stable and predictable regulatory framework for the next four years.

title: Latvia expands residential solar and battery rebate scheme - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Latvia has expanded its €85 million household renewable energy support program, raising grants for eligible households and increasing the minimum supported battery capacity from 5 kWh to 10 kWh. The scheme had supported 15,700 projects as of May 2026, including more than 14,000 applications for solar PV and over 2,000 for battery storage.
Emiliano Bellini
07 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Energy Storage
Highlights
Residential
Riga, Latvia
Latvia’s Ministry of Climate and Energy has expanded its household renewable energy support program, increasing financial support for eligible households installing technologies including solar PV and battery energy storage systems.
For PV, households holding Latvia’s Goda ģimene family card will be eligible for grants covering up to 85% of eligible costs, up from 70%. The card is a government-backed benefit scheme for large families and families caring for a child with a disability.
The support program has a total budget of €85 million ($98.7 million), of which around €20 million remains available. Households can receive up to €15,000 per project, depending on the technologies installed and their capacity.
For battery storage, the government has increased the minimum eligible nominal capacity from 5 kWh to 10 kWh. The ministry said the change is intended to enable households to store more of their self-generated electricity for later use.
As of May 2026, the scheme had supported 15,700 projects, with more than €59.75 million awarded, according to the Latvian government. Solar PV was by far the most popular technology, with the ministry reporting more than 14,000 applications for solar panels, alongside more than 2,000 applications for batteries.
Latvia’s solar capacity has reached 1,521 MW
, according to statistics released by the Latvian Renewable Energy Alliance (LREA) in August.
The figure indicates around 601 MW of solar have been added in the country so far this year, adding to the
that were installed by the end of the last year. This growth trajectory means 2026 is already the most successful year for solar deployment in Latvia, outpacing the previous calendar record year of 319 MW in 2024.

title: Vietnam lays early policy groundwork to aggregate rooftop PV, storage, and EVs into VPPs - pv magazine Global
content: From ESS News Vietnam is preparing to transition its power system beyond basic Time-of-Use (TOU) tariffs and industrial demand response programs toward virtual power plants (VPPs). According to a publication by Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade (MOIT) via its Industry Agency and penned by Nguyen Huy Hoach, Scientific Council of the Vietnam Energy Journal, authorities are beginning to express early thoughts on aggregation platforms. The concept, one explored in many other regions , will aim to link what the country said will be distributed rooftop solar, behind-the-meter battery energy storage systems (BESS), and electric vehicles into flexible grid assets. By orchestrating thousands of distributed energy resources (DERs) through algorithmic dispatch and controls, grid operators can absorb potential midday PV generation, and dispatch stored energy during the evening peak. MOIT’s rapid public framing of VPPs is notable, with the country overbuilding solar , which led to severe grid bottlenecks and curtailment across central and southern provinces. The move, with MOIT outlining VPP aggregation, suggests potential benefits for the grid. Vietnam’s market architecture, with state utility EVN maintaining a near-monopoly on transmission and single-buyer dispatch, means that for VPPs to deliver real balance sheet viability, the country will need clear aggregation framework, under its market rules. “The remaining issue is to develop a suitable roadmap and mechanism so that dispersed resources can participate in the electricity market effectively and transparently,” MOIT said. content:

Solar Energy Corp. of India (SECI) has launched a tender for 700 MW of interstate transmission system (ISTS)-connected solar PV projects in special economic zones (SEZs) or areas designated as export-oriented units (EOUs) in India, with the electricity earmarked for a commercial and industrial (C&I) consumer in Odisha.
Uma Gupta
07 Sep 2026
Applications & Installations
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
Utility-scale
AMPIN Energy’s 135 MWp solar project for Amazon Web Services
Solar Energy Corp. of India (SECI) has invited bids to develop 700 MW of interstate transmission system (ISTS)-connected solar PV projects under the build-own-operate (BOO) model, with the power intended for commercial and industrial (C&I) consumption in Odisha.
Under the request for selection (RfS), SECI will sign 25-year power purchase agreements (PPAs) with successful bidders. The electricity procured from the projects is planned to be sold to an export-oriented unit (EOU) of a C&I buying entity located in Odisha.
SECI will act as an intermediary nodal agency, procuring electricity from selected solar power developers and selling it to the buying entity on a back-to-back basis. The details of buying entities will be intimated at a later date, according to the tender documents.
The tender requires the solar projects to be established within special economic zones (SEZs) or areas designated as export oriented units (EOUs) in India, to supply solar power to the buying entity having EOU in Odisha. The arrangement is intended to allow the projects to qualify for an exemption from the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) requirements in accordance with a May 2024 circular issued by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), as amended from time to time.
Developers will be responsible for land acquisition, project development, as well as obtaining grid connectivity and constructing the transmission network up to the interconnection or delivery point.
Selection of solar PV projects for a total capacity of 700 MW will be carried out through e-bidding followed by e-Reverse auction process. Bids can be made for a minimum contracted capacity of 50 MW and a maximum quantum of 700 MW. A single project can be set up at multiple locations with different delivery points.

title: Zambia's PV capacity tops 841 MW - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Zambia’s installed solar PV capacity has surged from 88 MW in 2021 to approximately 841 MW in 2026, including around 584 MW of identified utility-scale projects and 30 MW under net metering.
Emiliano Bellini
07 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
Residential
Utility-scale
The 136 MW Itimpi II PV plant is currently Zambia’s largest operational solar facility.
‘s Ministry of Energy has announced that the country’s cumulative installed solar PV capacity reached approximately 841 MW by the end of July 2026.
“Solar power has grown remarkably from only 88 MW in 2021 to approximately 841 MW in 2026, placing Zambia firmly on course to achieve the target of 1,000 MW of solar generation by the end of this year, in line with the Presidential Directive,” the ministry said during a press briefing on the electricity sector.
Of the country’s installed PV capacity, around 30 MW is currently operating under Zambia’s net metering regime, which was launched in July 2024.
The net metering framework allows eligible consumers to install grid-connected renewable energy systems, particularly solar PV, for self-consumption and to export surplus electricity to the grid through bi-directional meters.
Utility-scale solar accounts for a significant share of Zambia’s expanding PV fleet.
Major projects include Copperbelt Energy Corporation’s (CEC) 60 MW Itimpi Phase I and 136 MW Itimpi Phase II solar plants in Kitwe; ZESCO’s
100 MW Chisamba Solar Phase I and 100 MW Chisamba Solar Phase II projects
, as well as the 50 MW Mabumba solar plant in Mansa; the 25 MW Mailo Phase I and 35 MW Mailo Phase II Solar Century projects in Serenje; the 20 MW Kiyona NRDC solar project; the 15 MW Kasupe Phase I and II projects; the 16 MW Northrise Lifesong solar project; and the 27 MW Lunsemfwa solar project.
Together, these utility-scale projects represent approximately 584 MW of capacity. When combined with the roughly 30 MW installed under the net metering regime, the identified capacity amounts to around 614 MW, leaving a difference of approximately 227 MW compared with the government’s reported national total of 841 MW. The Ministry of Energy has not provided a breakdown of the remaining capacity or clarified which installations are included in this portion of the total.

title: Europe's PV waste could yield up to 63 GW of new solar capacity - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Recovering silicon from Europe’s end-of-life solar panels won’t meaningfully cut import reliance unless the region’s ingot and wafer manufacturing base grows to absorb it, a SINTEF Industry researcher tells pv magazine.
Brian Publicover
07 Sep 2026
Research & Development
recycling
A new SINTEF Industry study estimates secondary silicon recovered from end-of-life crystalline silicon PV modules could support 35.6 GW to 62.9 GW of new solar manufacturing capacity in the European Union by 2040, though researchers say Europe’s limited ingot and wafer industry remains the key bottleneck.
Nagarajan Somi Ganesan, a researcher at SINTEF Industry, said the European Union could generate between 71.4 kilotons and 125.8 kilotons of secondary silicon from end-of-life crystalline silicon PV waste by 2040, enough to manufacture an estimated 35.6 to 62.9 GW of new PV capacity. SINTEF is one of Europe’s largest independent research institutes, based in Norway.
Somi Ganesan said Europe’s ability to utilize recovered silicon domestically depends on the successful expansion of its upstream PV supply chain.
“Several ingot and wafer projects, including Sunwaf in Spain (20 GW) and BEE Solar/Huasun in Italy (3 GW), indicate growing manufacturing capacity,” he said. “If realized, recovered silicon from end-of-life PV modules could help reduce reliance on primary silicon.”
He said that while recovered silicon’s current purity level (2N-3N) is already suitable for applications like Al-Si alloys and silicones, putting it to higher-value use in PV manufacturing itself will require Europe to build out further upgrading and refining capabilities.
Sunwaf is targeting 20 GW in Spain, with construction expected to begin in 2027 and commercial operations set for early 2029. A 3 GW ingot and wafer facility under BEE Solar or Huasun in Italy could not be confirmed. Documented Huasun-linked activity in Italy relates to approximately 1 GW of tandem and module production rather than upstream ingot and wafer capacity.
The study’s forecast depends heavily on assumed silicon recovery and refining efficiencies. Somi Ganesan said the paper assumes a 75% recovery efficiency and a subsequent 75% refining efficiency to upgrade recovered silicon to polysilicon grade.
“These values are based on published literature and represent plausible future performance rather than current industry-wide practice,” he said. “To account for uncertainty, the interactive EoL-PV dashboard developed from this work allows users to vary recovery and refining efficiencies and directly assess their impact on the projected results.”
The study’s net waste estimates come in below some other widely cited EU forecasts, a gap Somi Ganesan attributed to methodology rather than more optimistic underlying assumptions about gross waste generation.
“The main reason our estimates differ from some widely cited EU PV waste forecasts is that we report net EoL PV waste, not just gross waste generation,” he said. “While gross waste estimates are broadly comparable (4.63-10.63 Mt by 2040 in our study versus 5.0-9.8 Mt reported by Kastanaki et al. (2025)), our net estimates account for an 85% collection rate and the reuse of a share of younger modules. Specifically, we assume that 50% of collected modules younger than 15 years are refurbished and redeployed for a second life of at least 10 years. As a result, these modules do not enter the waste stream during the 2020-2040 period, leading to lower net waste quantities than forecasts that consider only gross EoL generation.”
Asked which assumption, collection efficiency or second-life reuse, has the greater effect on the study’s projections, Somi Ganesan said second-life reuse carries more weight.
“Second-life reuse has a greater impact because it delays waste generation beyond 2040, whereas collection efficiency only affects the fraction of waste entering the formal collection system,” he said.
The scientists discussed their findings in “
Future crystalline silicon PV waste generation and secondary silicon availability in the European Union
,” which was published in
Solar Energy Materials and Solar Cells
, Volume 307 (December 2026). The research team included Somi Ganesan, as well as colleagues Birgit Ryningen, Berhane Darsene Dimd, Yijiang Xu, and Martin Bellmann.

title: Uzbekistan has now 2.5 GW of solar under net metering - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Uzbekistan added 509.7 MW of PV capacity under its Solar House net metering scheme in the first eight months of 2026.
Emiliano Bellini
07 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Asia-Pacific
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
Residential
Uzbekistan deployed 2,508 MW of PV capacity under its
Solar House net metering scheme
between April 2023 and August 2026, according to the Uzbek Ministry of Energy.
The Solar House program was introduced in April 2023 to encourage households to install solar arrays of up to 50 kW. Under the scheme, residential prosumers receive a state subsidy of UZS 1,000 ($0.08)/kWh for surplus electricity supplied to the grid.
The subsidy is calculated monthly based on the positive difference between electricity exported to and imported from the grid, with payments made to participants through a dedicated mobile app. Households whose monthly exports exceed consumption do not pay an electricity bill for that month.
Newly installed PV capacity under the scheme reached 509.7 MW in the first eight months of 2026.
Based on the current pace of deployment, the government expects 700 MW of new capacity to be commissioned in 2026, exceeding its annual target by 300 MW. This would bring Uzbekistan’s total installed small-scale solar capacity to 2.7 GW by the end of the year.
The Uzbek government is targeting 25 GW of combined solar and wind capacity by 2030.

title: Mongolia completes first renewable energy auction - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
The auction procured 220 MW of solar and 135 MW/440 MWh of battery energy storage across five projects. A second auction, covering renewable energy projects with a stabilisation solution in Mongolia’s Gobi region, is scheduled to take place on September 11.
Patrick Jowett
07 Sep 2026
Applications & Installations
Markets & Policy
Asia-Pacific
Commercial & industrial
Energy Storage
Highlights
Utility-scale
Mongolia’s National Dispatching Centre, its state-owned electricity system operator, has signed power purchase agreements with the winning bidders from the country’s first competitive renewable energy auction.
The auction awarded 220 MW of solar PV capacity and 135 MW/440 MWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) across five provinces. The five individual lots consisted of four 50 MW solar plus 30 MW/100 MWh BESS projects in the provinces of Bulgan, Uvurkhangai, Govisumber and Dundgovi, and a 20 MW solar plus 15 MW/40 MWh BESS in the province of Khentii.
The auction took place earlier this year, attracting interest from 115 domestic and international companies. There were a total 19 qualified bidders following technical evaluations, with five selected to carry out the projects. Winning tariffs ranged from $0.0485/kWh in Dundgovi to $0.078/kWh in Khentii.
According to a recent post published by the Mongolian government, each of the projects is expected to be operational before peak winter demand season.
Mongolia’s Prime Minister, Nyam-Osoryn Uchral, added that the auction results reflect growing investor confidence in Mongolia and demonstrates the government’s commitment to opening the energy sector to greater competition and private investment.
The country’s Ministry of Energy has announced a second renewable energy auction will take place on September 11.
invitation to participate
explains that the ministry is seeking an independent power producer to develop renewable energy projects with a stabilisation solution capable of supplying Mongolia’s Gobi region with electricity at 99.5% reliability.
The invitation states two specified connection points, a 220/110/35 kV substation and distribution facility and a 220 kV open switchgear facility, both within the province of Ömnögovi. The auction does not state a targeted procurement capacity.
The auction is open to both domestic and international developers, although foreign companies must establish a consortium with a Mongolian-registered national company that sees the Mongolian company holding the majority share.
A bid bond of $5,000 per MW of renewable capacity has been set. The ministry explicitly states no bid is required for the stabilisation solution or for the power and capacity of any BESS.
Analysis published by
pv magazine
earlier this year explained Mongolia’s
growing renewable energy sector
is driven by efforts to diversify its coal-based energy mix and tap export opportunities in neighboring China.
Mongolia’s cumulative solar capacity stood at 129 MW at the end of last year, according to figures published by the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), down on the 143 MW reported at the end of the year prior.

title: Water-jet guided laser cuts high-temperature  alloys with 99% less heat damage
content: A technique called Water-Jet Guided Laser (WJGL) technology could solve a major hurdle in manufacturing advanced high-strength metals known as refractory high-entropy alloys. Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are the absolute rock stars of modern metallurgy. These materials can survive in hellish environments that would melt standard nickel superalloys, making them essential for next-generation aerospace engines, nuclear reactors, and gas turbines. However, the high hardness, brittleness, and poor thermal conductivity make RHEA difficult to machine, as standard high-power lasers cause severe thermal shock, cracking, oxidation, and slag. Water-Jet Guided Laser technology overcomes this challenge by channeling a laser inside a microscopic jet of water to precisely cut the material while simultaneously cooling the surface and clearing away debris. In testing, the team from China reduced heat damage by over 99 percent, preventing structural defects and enabling flawless, highly precise micro-components for extreme environments like aerospace engines and nuclear reactors. Eliminating the burn zone WJGL technology is a precision manufacturing method that couples a high-power laser inside a microscopic, 50-micrometer stream of high-pressure water surrounded by protective shielding gas. The water jet acts as a liquid optical waveguide because of the refractive-index difference between the water core and the gas cladding. This design continually reflects the laser inside the stream via total internal reflection, overcoming the need for focal-point or Rayleigh-length adjustments. This hybrid approach simultaneously integrates three key functions: laser ablation, in-situ water cooling, and real-time debris scouring. It reduces thermal damage, washes away melted residue, and delivers exceptionally clean, highly accurate micromachining. Water-Jet Guided Laser technology provides three distinct processing advantages over other lasers when machining hard-to-process alloys . First, the continuous scouring action of the water jet removes slag and oxidized sputtering residues, producing a clean processing interface with smooth inner walls and vertical groove profiles. Then the real triumph lies in how little damage the process leaves behind. When conventional nanosecond lasers (CNL) slice into RHEAs , the tech cooks the surrounding metal, creating a massive “Heat-Affected Zone” (HAZ) up to 31.6 micrometers wide. This thermal injury could severely weaken the component. WJGL collapses that damaged margin down to a razor-thin 298 to 702 nanometers, a 99.1 percent reduction in thermal impact. The water shielding prevents the hot metal from reacting with oxygen in the air by keeping the heat strictly confined to the target zone. The internal microstructure of the alloy remains pristine. Finally, the uniform distribution of laser energy inside the liquid waveguide enables ultra-low taper drilling, maintaining high consistency and less than 1 micron of surface roughness variation in deep micro-holes with a taper as low as 0.014°. Better than existing methods Standard laser setups force engineers to constantly worry about focal lengths, beam intensity, and thermal buildup. Using a liquid waveguide, water-jet guided laser technology eliminates the need to manage focal-point positioning or Rayleigh length, allowing the laser beam to travel with consistent intensity over much longer distances. This stabilized energy delivery, combined with immediate in-situ cooling, effectively solves the severe thermal damage, microcracking, and structural defects that typically plague alloys during conventional nanosecond and femtosecond laser micromachining. Ultimately, WJGL will provide a reliable, high-precision manufacturing route for RHEAs, preserving the alloy’s intrinsic mechanical properties for applications in aerospace, nuclear power , and gas turbines.

title: New ground robot joins software platform that also powers aerial drones
content: Robots are increasingly being used to help people carry out tasks in places that may be dangerous, difficult, or time-consuming to reach. Israeli physical AI firm XTEND has now expanded its robotics business from flying systems to ground-based machines with the first delivery of its AtlasROVER robot to a customer in the Asia-Pacific region. The AtlasROVER is the first robot from Atlas to use XTEND’s XOS operating software. XOS is designed to work with different types of robots and give them shared tools, including AI features, task-specific applications, and controls for human operators. XTEND says the move is part of a larger plan to create one software system for robots that operate in the air, on the ground, and eventually at sea. XOS meets AtlasROVER XTEND has expanded its XOS robotics operating system from aerial platforms into ground-based systems with the deployment of an AtlasROVER robot to a customer in the Asia-Pacific region. The deployment is the first XOS-powered AtlasROVER system XTEND has delivered since acquiring Latvia-based robotics company Atlas earlier this year. It also shows XTEND’s broader effort to use XOS as a common software layer across different types of robotic platforms. AtlasROVER is designed to operate in challenging environments and can carry different mission-specific payloads, according to XTEND. The company has not disclosed the identity or location of the customer, the number of robots delivered, or the specific mission covered by the contract. The deployment therefore offers limited information about the operational role of the platform, but highlights XTEND’s efforts to bring its software architecture beyond drones and into ground robotics. At the center of the integration is XOS, which XTEND describes as a hardware-agnostic operating system for physical AI and human-guided autonomy. Rather than developing separate software environments for each robotic platform, the system is intended to provide a common framework for AI capabilities, mission applications, and operator workflows. According to XTEND, it allows different robotic systems to operate through a shared software architecture while retaining their platform-specific hardware and capabilities. XTEND unifies robotics The integration of AtlasROVER gives XTEND a ground platform that can operate within the same broader XOS ecosystem as its aerial robotic systems. The approach could let operators use familiar interfaces and mission tools across different machine types, rather than learning separate control systems for every platform. XTEND says the architecture is intended to support cooperation between different robotic platforms while keeping humans involved in important operational decisions. The Atlas acquisition has expanded the range of ground robotics available to XTEND and provides the company with additional engineering and manufacturing capabilities in Europe.  Following the acquisition, XTEND began integrating Atlas’ technology and deployed systems into its wider robotics portfolio. The AtlasROVER integration represents one of the first visible steps in applying XOS to this newly expanded ground-robotics portfolio. Building a common interface for autonomous systems For XTEND, the significance of the AtlasROVER deployment extends beyond the individual vehicle. The company is positioning XOS as a software foundation that can connect robots operating in different environments. While the system was initially developed around aerial robotics, extending it to ground platforms could help XTEND create a more unified ecosystem in which operators can manage different robotic assets through common tools and workflows. “Our goal is not to build isolated robotic products, but to create a common software layer that can extend across air, ground, and ultimately maritime systems,” said Aviv Shapira, CEO and co-founder of XTEND, in a statement . Such an expansion would make the software platform increasingly independent of any particular robotic form factor, with the underlying operating environment providing a common interface for human-guided autonomy. XTEND says it has deployed more than 12,500 systems across over 30 countries, including five active combat zones. The company employs nearly 300 people, with more than half based in Israel. It also operates manufacturing facilities in the UK, Singapore, and Latvia, in addition to its production site in Tampa.

title: Wheeled robot dog takes on sand, slopes and unforgiving desert terrain
content: DEEP Robotics has released footage showing its Lynx wheel-legged robot series navigating harsh desert terrain, highlighting its ability to operate across challenging environments. The demonstration focuses on the robot’s off-road mobility as it tackles uneven and demanding landscapes that can pose difficulties for conventional wheeled machines. Developed by Hangzhou-based DEEP Robotics, the Lynx series is designed for industrial applications where robots may need to operate in hazardous or inaccessible areas. The latest footage underscores the company’s push to develop versatile robotic systems capable of handling complex terrain for industrial, exploration, and emergency operations.Lynx masters terrainDEEP Robotics has released new footage showing its Lynx wheel-legged robot navigating a harsh red desert terrain, highlighting the machine’s ability to operate across loose sand, steep slopes, and uneven ground.The footage features the Lynx M20 series, an industrial-grade wheel-legged robot designed for applications in hazardous and difficult-to-access environments. Unlike conventional quadruped robots that rely entirely on legs, the Lynx combines wheels and articulated legs to provide different forms of mobility depending on the terrain.The demonstration, titled “Conquering the Red Desert,” features the company’s industrial quadruped tackling conditions that can be difficult for conventional wheeled robots. In the video, the robot travels across sandy and uneven surfaces while negotiating changes in elevation and ground conditions. Its hybrid mobility system allows it to roll across relatively smooth sections while using its articulated legs to adapt to more difficult terrain. This approach is intended to combine the efficiency and speed of wheeled movement with the obstacle-clearing capabilities associated with legged robots.The demonstration also highlights the Lynx platform’s ability to maintain mobility in dusty, high-temperature environments. DEEP says the system is designed to withstand temperatures as high as 55 degrees Celsius (131 degrees Fahrenheit), a capability that could be relevant for industrial operations in some of the world’s harshest environments.The company is positioning the Lynx M20 series for tasks where sending people into the field can present significant safety challenges. Potential applications include inspections at power facilities, emergency response, firefighting, search and rescue, and scientific exploration.Robot braves extremesDesert operations are only one part of the platform’s reported testing. DEEP has also demonstrated the Lynx in extreme cold, with tests reaching temperatures as low as minus 30 degrees Celsius (minus 22 degrees Fahrenheit). The robot has additionally been shown crossing icy waterways with depths of up to 80 centimeters, underscoring the company’s focus on developing machines capable of operating across widely varying environments.The Lynx’s wheel-legged configuration is central to this strategy. Wheels can provide faster and more energy-efficient movement on suitable surfaces, while the legs can help the robot adjust its body position and negotiate obstacles when rolling alone becomes impractical. This gives the platform greater flexibility when operating across terrain that can change rapidly over short distances.DEEP Robotics describes the Lynx M20 series as the world’s first industrial-grade wheeled-legged robot built specifically for challenging terrain and hazardous industrial environments. The company’s approach reflects a wider effort within the robotics industry to develop machines capable of performing inspection, response, and exploration tasks without requiring humans to directly enter dangerous areas.The Lynx series is commercially available for industrial customers, with prices starting at around $17,999. With its latest desert demonstration, DEEP Robotics is continuing to emphasize real-world deployment as it seeks to establish wheel-legged robots as practical tools for demanding field operations.

title: China completes 690-foot tunnel on railway designed to bypass Russia
content: China has reached a key construction milestone on the long-delayed China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan (CKU) railway, with workers drilling through the first tunnel on the Kyrgyz section as Beijing pushes ahead with a major trade route across Central Asia.The 210-meter (690-foot) tunnel was completed in the Kyrgyz section after full-scale construction began in June 2025, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Saturday. Work on the section has now reached 17 percent.The development came shortly after Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Kyrgyzstan last week, where the two countries pledged to support the smooth construction of the railway. The project is a major component of China’s Belt and Road Initiative and is intended to create a route to markets farther west.Railway will cut across Central AsiaThe CKU railway will stretch for more than 500 kilometers (310 miles), including about 305 kilometers (190 miles) inside Kyrgyzstan. It will connect Kashgar in China’s western Xinjiang region with Andijan in Uzbekistan, crossing the mountainous terrain of Kyrgyzstan along the way.Once operational, the railway is expected to become the shortest overland connection between China and the Middle East and Europe. CCTV said it could reduce transit times by as much as eight days compared with the China-Europe Railway Express.The railway will also open a new trade route for southern Xinjiang. For landlocked Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, it will provide direct rail access toward Chinese and Asia-Pacific markets.Construction is already under way on 27 tunnels, 43 bridges and 88 roadbed sections. Work has also started at 20 planned railway stations, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua.Difficult terrain delayed the projectThe railway was first planned in 1997 but has faced decades of delays. Engineers struggled with tough mountain terrain, and disagreements over railway gauges added to the challenges.The project is also important geopolitically because it gives China a route that avoids the usual corridors through Russia and Kazakhstan. As China’s economic influence in Central Asia grows, Moscow has taken notice of the railway’s development.Kyrgyzstan has increasingly sought alternative sources of foreign investment as Russia’s regional influence faces pressure from the prolonged war in Ukraine, according to a Times of Central Asia report published during Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov’s visit to Beijing last year.At the same time, Russia and China continue to expand their economic relationship. Russian outlet Izvestia reported on Sunday that Moscow is upgrading existing rail crossings and considering new highways to handle growing bilateral trade.Two rail gauges will meetThe CKU project has adopted a dual-gauge design to resolve the long-standing technical dispute. About 167.5 kilometers (104 miles) from the Chinese border to Makmal will use China’s standard railway gauge.The remaining section of nearly 140 kilometers (87 miles) toward Uzbekistan will use the Soviet-era broad gauge. Cargo will be transferred between systems at a planned hub in Makmal.“The significance of this arrangement is that China’s… standard gauge enters the heart of Central Asia for the first time,” Li Lifan, director of the Center for Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Studies at the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, told CCTV.China, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Russia are all members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, which celebrated its 25th anniversary at a leadership summit in Bishkek last week.Completion targets remain disputedProject chief engineer Xi Jihong said the railway could be ready for operations by June 2031. Uzbekistan, however, wants construction to move faster.Deputy Transport Minister Jasurbek Choriev said in June that Uzbekistan aimed to accelerate the work and complete the railway by 2028, according to the Tashkent Times.The different deadlines highlight the pressure surrounding a project that has remained on the drawing board for decades. The successful drilling of the first Kyrgyz tunnel now provides a tangible sign that construction is moving forward.
